VII. ANY IRREVERSIBLE AND IRRETRIEVABLE COMMITMENTS OF RESOURCES WHICH WOULD BE INVOLVED IN THE PROPOSED ACTION SHOULD IT BE IMPLEMENTED
The total extent of resources, either natural or man made, which will be irreversibly committed as a result of the proposed action, is limited compared to the benefits that will be derived from the proposed improvement. The resources committed generally include the following:
A. Land Resources Lost to Right-of-Way Acquisition for this Proposal.
With the proposed urban cross section and the elimination of open side ditch drainage, the land resource commitment to right-of-way is as follows:
....From Cicero to Western Avenue a width of 116 feet is generally required. The existing width varies from 66 to 160 feet. Approximately 12.4 acres of land will be acquired.
....From Western Avenue to Edgewood Avenue a width of 92 feet is generally required, however this width will be reduced where feasible in order to avoid building acquisitions. The existing width varies from 66 to 83 feet. Approximately 3.5 acres of land will be acquired.
....From Edgewood Avenue to Aberdeen Street a width of 76.5 feet is generally required. The existing right-of-way is 69.5 feet. Approximately 0.10 acres of land will be acquired.
....At the Roosevelt School approximately 0.20 acres of land will be acquired. (See Chapter V, Section K.)
....From the Cook County Forest Preserve District approximately 0.17 acres of land will be required for a "temporary construction easement". (See Chapter V, Section F and Chapter VII, Section B.)
B. Use of Section 4(f) Lands
The State of Illinois Department of Transportation will require the temporary use of less than 0.2 acres of land for the removal of wingwalls from the bridge over Thorn Creek and to provide a safer grade for the entrance driveway into the Cook County Forest Preserve District site, located in the northwest quadrant of the intersection between Lincoln Highway and Chicago Road.
This is not total committment of a land resource, however, it will take a period of time, even with the help of manpower and nature, for the land to return to its original condition.
